name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 24 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA says the fourth global coral bleaching event likely ended in 2025 after heat stress reached 84.4% of reef area, and no fifth event has been declared (NOAA). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report in August warned reef cover risks irreversible decline (Al Jazeera, 31 Aug), and El Niño conditions could bring another event (bdnews24, 2 Nov). No new global declaration was found on 24 Nov, so Normal holds with risk rising as the very strong El Niño persists.
for_you: No global bleaching event is declared. Coastal communities that rely on reef fishing and tourism in the tropics are most exposed if El Niño heat triggers new bleaching in the coming months.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress per NOAA Coral Reef Watch

sources.title: NOAA NESDIS — World's fourth mass coral bleaching event likely ended in 2025
Al Jazeera — Global coral reef coverage risks irreversible decline, new report warns

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
